newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN CASTORSEED SLUMPS, OVERSEAS BUYERS BACK OFF.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN CASTORSEED SLUMPS, OVERSEAS BUYERS BACK OFF.

text.p: Castorseed September delivery nosedived to 1,154/1,155 rupees per quintal from 1,170 rupees on the back of heavy unloading by the speculators, floor sources said.
Absence of fresh overseas enquiries arrested buying by the shipper while improved arrivals prompted heavy bull liquidation.
Daily arrivals of castorseed in the Gujarat region rose to 10,000/12,000 bags (75 kg each). No trading was reported in the castorseed December delivery due to lack of interest among traders.
"We are now concentrating on the maturing September delivery," one operator said.
Meanwhile groundnut oil was steady at 379/380 rupees per 10 kg amid limited arrivals but fresh seasonal demand was at a low ebb.
"Availability of imported edible oils at cheaper levels has curtailed fresh buying for groundnut oil at the higher level," one miller said.
In Rajkot spot groundnut oil was steady at 588/590 rupees per 15 kg.
Meanwhile, Bombay imported palm oil rose by one to two rupees to 260/261 rupees per 10 kg on the back of festival buying and rally in the world market.
"The price rise may prove shortlived looking at the rising arrivals of palm oil at Bombay port," one broker said.
